08 · Valuation Discipline

Same company. Different underwriting environment.

stripe
$0B
2021 · Series H
$0B
2023 · Series I
$0.0B
Sep 2025 · reported tender
$0B
2026 · Stripe tender
1 · Company performanceVolume, product breadth, enterprise adoption, and profitability continued to improve.
2 · Market multiplesHigher rates and lower private-market risk appetite compressed fintech valuations in 2022–23.
3 · Operating correctionStripe acknowledged pandemic-era overhiring and restructured in 2022.
4 · Transaction structure2021, 2023, 2025, and 2026 are not identical instruments or valuation contexts.
Important: $106.7B (Sep 2025) is press-reported, not a direct Stripe announcement. These are valuation references across different transaction types—not equivalent funding rounds. The reset was a re-pricing, not proof Stripe lost product-market fit.

09 · Competitive Advantage

The API was the wedge. The accumulated system became the moat.

stripe
More copyable
Harder to replicate
API design
Developer UX
Embedded workflows
Fraud / data
Bank / network relations
Regulatory coverage
Switching costs
Feature moatWeak by itself. APIs and checkout features can be imitated.
Infrastructure moatStronger. Relationships, compliance, data, integrations, and workflows take years to accumulate.
Platform effectConnect and multi-product adoption embed Stripe deeper into customers’ operating systems.
The moat is cumulative, not singular.
